frontier.mechanism: sched.c:2536 `return (reg_n_sets[i] == 1);` inside birthing_insn_p is the ONLY remaining condition in the LAUNCH_PRIORITY path that C source can change: reload_completed is fixed by which scheduling pass is running, the (set (reg) ...) pattern shape is fixed by the program's meaning, and bb_live_regs is now MEASURED to be unconditionally set for a live load (s7, birth=1). Setting reg_n_sets to 2 requires two live writes of the p10 local - the banned carrier, which is also the construct that reaches score 0 (rejected/banned-temp2-dual-role-score0-layer1-and-judge-FAIL.c).

frontier.hypothesis: cb's defect can be closed from the REGISTER-ALLOCATION side rather than the scheduling side: if local-alloc/global-alloc gave p10's pseudo $a1 instead of $v0, sched2 - which never bumps - could hoist the load from slot 23 to slot 11 and cb would match, with no second write anywhere.
frontier.mechanism: sched2 runs with reload_completed == 1, so birthing_insn_p returns 0 at sched.c:2509 and the bump is absent; the only thing preventing the hoist in cb is that $v0 is written at slot 20 and read at slot 22, straddling the gap. In the target the same load sits in $a1, which is dead from slot 11 to slot 28, so the hoist is legal there. This is a DIFFERENT gate from reg_n_sets: s10 raised the v0-vs-a0 question, but s6 folded it into the scheduling story and no session has read .lreg/.greg for a 3-load body.
